summary: Round 5 red team of the private-only failure modes of the two finals, K2 (exp58) and the twin (exp58n). Checked at the code level against the logs of the 56 real exp60 lab clips, the 7 dummy runs and a new smoke test. No real bug was found, so no rebuild is justified and nothing needs doing before the finals beyond the existing READ TABLE. (1) A crash only on private clips cannot happen: one hidden rerun covers public and private together (step0.md l.19-20). #34, #35 and P36 COMPLETE therefore prove that the x138 core and the insertion code do not crash on any private clip. #37 and #38 COMPLETE will prove the same for lowrefine and safetail. The only remaining risk is a silent per-clip fallback, which is invisible on both public and private. (2) The notebooks differ from #35 in only three places: the cell-0 knobs, the lowrefine lines and safetail. In #35 and P36 the insertion was not locally fail-soft: an insertion exception sent the whole clip to REPAIR FAILED and the fallback graph. K2 reverts only the insertion, and the revert is exact because insert_divisions does not mutate its inputs. So K2 is at least as safe as #35. (3) lowrefine: the V1284 refine is stateless (its cache holds only the head weights), bounded below 2 um and wrapped in a per-frame try. It cannot raise outside that try and cannot affect the main refine. A float-pool smoke test ran K2's own readmit and gap-filler code on the 56 lab ILP graphs: 0 exceptions, 0 non-fatal or idle messages. Predict time with lowrefine is 9.30/9.40 min vs 9.18-10.59 min without, which is noise. (4) On the 56 real lab clips every failure counter is 0 (repair_fallback, deadline_degraded, relink fallback or large-frame skip, DeepCenter missing, short-track skip-all). The ILP maximum is 67.5 s against a 1,200 s timeout, the repair maximum is 417 s per clip and insertion scoring averages 52 s per clip (max 290 s). (5) Residual risks, all bounded and already covered by the table: both finals share lowrefine, but its reach is about 1% of nodes and its effect is below ~5e-4. If the 8.0 h insertion deadline fires, it only turns K2 into the twin on the last-sorted clips. The large-loss path is the 9.5 h degrade, which has a forecast margin of 1.63 h.

findings.what: A crash that happens only on private clips cannot occur for K2 or the twin. Kaggle reruns the notebook ONCE over the whole hidden test (public embryo plus private embryos) and scores one submission.csv. Any kernel-level exception on a private clip would therefore have shown as an ERROR on #34, #35 or P36. All three are COMPLETE. So the x138 core, the retention guard, the DeepCenter and the ILP, the writer and the guard cells, and the DaughterNet insertion code (same code and params as K2) handled every private clip without a crash. If #37 and #38 are COMPLETE, the same holds for lowrefine and safetail. What remains is silent per-clip degradation: REPAIR FAILED, DIVINS FAILED/SKIPPED, LOWREFINE FAILED, readmit skipped. Hidden-run logs are not visible, so this cannot be observed on public or on private. It is not a private-specific risk.

findings.what: Fail-soft asymmetry between #35/P36 and K2. The exp57b (#35) notebook calls the insertion inside filter_output_graph WITHOUT its own try, so any insertion exception on a hidden clip triggered the per-dataset except, which prints 'REPAIR FAILED' and writes fallback_output_graph (the ILP graph with basic filtering, no relink, gap closing, safe divisions or short-track filter). K2 wraps the insertion in try/except and reverts only the insertion (edges = _dv_edges_in). The revert is exact because insert_divisions never mutates its inputs: it builds a new list and removes steals by id(). So on every clip K2 >= #35 in failure behaviour. Consequence for reading: a positive d1 = K2 - #35 could come partly from this rather than from lowrefine. The probability is tiny (0 insertion exceptions in the 4 dummies and 56 lab clips) and the READ TABLE acts only on d1 <= -0.002, so no rule changes.

FF dummy: CSV byte-identical to exp56 (CONTEXT 25 Sep 17:45).
findings.action: Info only. When reading d1, remember it also carries this (tiny) safety term. No build and no rule change.

findings.what: Code audit of lowrefine, the only component of BOTH finals that no scored LB file has run on the hidden set. (a) v1284 refine() keeps no state across calls (the module-level _CACHE holds only the head weights, mean and scale). The lowdet call runs before the main refine in the same frame and cannot change the main peaks. (b) The shift is bounded below 2 um by construction, the result is clipped to the feature grid, and it raises only on non-finite values. That call and the shape/t-column check sit inside the per-frame try, and a failure restores #35's grid coordinates. (c) Code outside the try (astype, counters, append, the float32 dump) cannot raise on empty frames, because of the len(_low) and _lhi.any() guards and refine's own len(arr)==0 return. (d) NEW smoke test: K2's own cell-7 functions (build_low_detection_pool, load_low_detections, readmit_discarded_detections, fill_gaps_from_low_detections) were exec'd with K2's knobs on the 56 real exp60 ILP geffs. Two pools were compared: the lab int16 pool (as in #35) and a float32 pool where peaks with score >= 0.965 were moved up to 1.9 um in random directions (like lowrefine). Result: 0 exceptions and 0 'skipped/idle/unreadable' messages in both arms; readmit 18,178 vs 18,888. (e) Predict time on the dummies is within noise: K2 9.30 min and twin 9.40 min vs 9.18-10.59 min without lowrefine.

findings.what: What actually happens on real clips (56 exp60 lab clips, nearly the K2 stack minus lowrefine; the insertion was scored but in dump-only mode at threshold 1.5): every failure counter is 0. That covers repair_fallback (no REPAIR FAILED), deadline_degraded, motion_relink_fallback_raw, motion_relink_skipped_large_frame, deepcenter_gap_missing, deepcenter_safe_div_missing, short_track_filter_skipped_all, gap_skipped_node_cap, gap2_skipped_cap and safe_division_skipped_cap. There are no Tracebacks and failed_hooks = 0. The only nonzero counters are benign: gap_refine_failed 14 on one clip (44b6_0db75fae; the synthetic midpoint is kept) and linefit_skipped_nodes 92. Scale headroom: raw nodes range 4,609-75,544 per clip (46-755 per frame); ILP max 67.5 s at 98,233 candidate nodes against the 1,200 s timeout (the K2 dummy max is 79.4 s at 76,396); repair max 417 s per clip, mean 91 s; DaughterNet scoring 52 s per clip, max 290 s at 34,794 scored nodes. The retention guard falls back to the primary seed on 100/100 frames in some 44b6 clips (x138's own deterministic rule, which also ran on the hidden set). A private clip would need roughly 15x the densest lab clip to reach the ILP timeout. #34 and #35 already processed every private clip at their latencies.

findings.what: F1 and F2 share lowrefine and safetail, so the f2 twin hedges only the insertion. The shared risk is small. lowrefine moves only lowdet-pool coordinates of peaks with score >= 0.965, which feed readmit and gapfill. On the dummies readmit went from 1,337 to 1,365 (+28 nodes of 121,252), gapfill from 110 to 111, and final nodes changed by +0.004/+0.118/0/+0.013 % per clip. Upper-bound arithmetic: at most ~1.2% of nodes (readmitted plus gapfill) change position by up to 2 um, against a 7 um match radius. Even if 10% of those flipped between matched and unmatched, the node and edge effect is about 0.1% of the graph, i.e. |delta score| <~ 5e-4 on any embryo. That is at least 10x smaller than the insertion's lab upper bound (+0.0065) that the twin hedges. The shared safetail is inert unless a deadline fires (the K1 sha equals the exp57b dummy).

findings.action: No change. The pair design (F1 = K2, F2 = twin) is right. The only lowrefine exits remain READ TABLE rows 4/5 and C4 (d1 or d2 <= -0.002). Do not add a third lowrefine-free candidate on this argument.

findings.what: The deadline paths with the insertion on, re-read for private exposure. Clips are processed in sorted stem order (sorted geffs). The 8.0 h insertion gate and the 9.5 h repair degrade are checked when each clip starts, so if either fires it hits the LAST-sorted clips, which may all belong to one private embryo. (a) The 8.0 h gate only turns K2 into the twin on those clips: the loss is at most (fraction skipped) x (insertion effect); for example, 5% of clips x the public +0.001 is about 5e-5, and it can never fall below the twin. (b) The 9.5 h degrade (no relink, no gap closing, no gap2, but safe divisions and linefit kept) is the only large-loss path. Forecast F(K2) = 7.87 h gives a 1.63 h margin. The twin runs about 1.3 h faster (it has no DaughterNet scoring, ~52 s per clip), so it is exposed much less. C6 'clean' (L(K2) <= 8.0 h) is a sufficient proof for BOTH public and private, because they share the run and runtime <= latency. The FD dummy exercised degrade plus insertion-skip on 4 clips, including the dense 6bba_05db0fb1 (76k nodes).

findings.action: At score time (A4 of round 4), note that 'clean' also certifies private. 'Not clean' costs at most K2 -> twin on the tail clips (row 5 logic stands). Raise the runtime trigger to the user only if L(K2) and L(twin) both suggest a runtime above ~9 h.

findings.what: Crash blast radius: x138's guard cells (cell 8 retention/topology guard; the cell 12 asserts on dt = 1, multi-parent, out-degree > 2 and the dataset set) and the CSV writer loop (int(round(nan)) on a NaN coordinate) are OUTSIDE the per-dataset try. Any topology or NaN anomaly on any single clip would therefore ERROR the whole submission instead of degrading one clip. The only K2 stage that adds edges after the tail is the insertion. By code it keeps in-degree <= 1, out-degree <= 2 and dt = 1: u has exactly one out-edge before, v is an orphan or its single in-edge is stolen, the used-set blocks reuse, and v is taken from t_u + 1. NaN cannot enter from lowrefine (isfinite check); readmit and gapfill copy finite pool coordinates. #35 and P36 already passed these guards on the full hidden set with the same insertion code and params. Verdict: this is a design property, not a bug.

findings.action: No action. Wrapping the guards or the writer in a per-clip fallback would be new code and a rebuild, which the evidence above does not justify: the expected value is ~0 because #35 and P36 already passed on the full hidden set.

findings.what: Idea considered and NOT recommended: a full end-to-end CPU replay of K2's cell 7 (relink, gap closing, safe divisions with the DeepCenter veto, short tracks, linefit, insertion with node_p from the divins dumps) from the 56 lab ILP geffs, with a lowrefine-like float pool, to measure REPAIR FAILED = 0 end to end. Mechanism: the same as the smoke test but covering the whole tail. Expected gain: 0 unless it finds a bug, and P(bug) is very small after the smoke test plus the 4 dummies plus #37/#38 COMPLETE. Cost: DeepCenter would need CPU torch inference on raw train frames, so several CPU hours; no GPU and no submission. Cheapest honest gate: none needed, because #37/#38 COMPLETE is stronger evidence against crashes, and silent fallbacks never appeared in 60 real clips.

findings.what: Answer to 'can or should anything still be done before the finals': NO rebuild, NO new build, NO submission from this red team. No real bug was found in any path the 4 dummies did not exercise: empty or near-empty frames, 0 detections, dense clips, lowdet pool edge cases, insertion with 0 candidates, the per-dataset REPAIR FAILED fallback, safetail degrade with the insertion on, memory and time, and the CSV writer. The only rebuild trigger would be a real bug shown by an ERROR on #37/#38, and READ TABLE row 1 / C2 already route that, K1 needing the user's OK. The finals default stays F1 = K2 #37 (56563521) and F2 = twin #38 (56563534), ticked by the provisional tick rule as soon as the table resolves.
